analysis.one_liner: Pidilite Industries makes adhesives, sealants and construction/craft chemicals — brands like Fevicol, Dr. Fixit and M-seal — sold to households, carpenters and masons, plus industrial customers.
analysis.whats_happening: Pidilite reports its September-2026 quarter (Q2 FY27) results on 28 October 2026, with the earnings call on 29 October — just days away. The last reported quarter (Q1 FY27, June 2026) showed revenue up 21% YoY to ₹4,552 crore and PAT up 30% YoY to ₹884 crore, with EBITDA margin expanding to 26.6%. Separately, the company named Amit Agarwal as CFO-designate from 9 October 2026, part of planned succession ahead of current CFO Sandeep Batra's scheduled retirement in 2027.
analysis.plain_terms: Pidilite makes the glue (Fevicol) and waterproofing/sealant products many Indian households and construction sites use, plus industrial chemicals sold to other businesses. The business has been growing briskly — both more volume sold and better margins — but a key raw material (vinyl acetate monomer, linked to the West Asia conflict) got a lot more expensive this year, so the company has been raising prices to protect profit. The tension to watch: can it keep growing volumes once prices rise, or does demand soften?
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (June 2026): revenue +21% YoY to ₹4,552 crore, PAT +30% YoY to ₹884 crore, EBITDA margin up ~152 bps YoY to 26.6% — above the company's usual 20-24% corridor. Management described this as volume-led, not just pricing: the core Consumer & Bazaar segment grew 22.5% YoY revenue with underlying volume growth of 12.2%; B2B grew 16% YoY with 7.3% volume growth. But vinyl acetate monomer (VAM), a key raw material, rose from about $924/tonne to $1,370/tonne amid the West Asia conflict, hitting gross margin by roughly 66 bps YoY and 313 bps sequentially — a cost-driven squeeze, not a demand problem. The company took calibrated price hikes of 2-12% across products to offset this. Q2 FY27 (September 2026 quarter) results land 28 October 2026 — too soon to know if the margin recovery held through the festive season.
analysis.performance_read: Over 1 year the stock is roughly flat (-1.2%) but still beat the Nifty, which fell 12.7% — relative resilience in a weak market, not an advance. Over 3 and 5 years it returned 30.4% and 33.8% respectively versus the Nifty's 18.2% and 24.7%, but in absolute terms a 5-year return of ~34% (roughly 6%/year) is modest for a business often described as a quality compounder — it has tracked rather than decisively outrun the market. The stock is down 12.6% from its August 2026 peak of ₹1,701.5, now at ₹1,487.7. Note: Pidilite did a 2:1 stock split in September 2025 (on top of earlier splits in 2005 and 2010) — a share-count adjustment, not a value event — and the price/return series already reflects it, so there is no hidden drawdown to add back.
analysis.valuation_read: At a consolidated P/E of roughly 57x and P/B of around 13x, Pidilite trades well above the broader chemicals sector (median P/E near 26x). Why it is expensive: a near debt-free balance sheet, ROCE of ~31% and ROE of ~24%, and a dominant, hard-to-replicate brand position in adhesives support a premium. Whether that premium is justified is separate — at 57x earnings the market is pricing in several more years of double-digit volume growth and stable-to-improving margins; a slip on either front (VAM costs staying elevated, or demand softening) would make the multiple look expensive in hindsight.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is currently both volume- and margin-led, the more durable combination. Q1 FY27 revenue grew 21% YoY with underlying volume growth of 12.2% in the core consumer business (not just price hikes), while EBITDA margin simultaneously expanded ~152 bps. That said, the company has had to take fresh price hikes (2-12%) to defend margin against a VAM cost spike, so some of this growth will depend on whether volumes hold once those price hikes fully work through.
analysis.health_read: Profits convert reasonably into cash for an asset-light consumer/specialty-chemicals business, and the balance sheet is almost debt-free (debt-to-equity ~0.04), so financial risk is minimal. The real risk here is business/input-cost risk — Pidilite is exposed to swings in petrochemical-linked raw materials like VAM, which recently jumped roughly 48% due to the West Asia conflict, and management has had to repeatedly lean on pricing to defend margin rather than benefiting from structurally lower costs.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold 69.18% with 0% pledged — a clean, stable position. Institutional interest is tilting more foreign: FII holding rose from 11.69% to 12.42% in the September 2026 quarter, while domestic mutual fund holding eased slightly (4.33% to 3.92%); DIIs overall hold around 9%. No well-known individual value investor was found on the shareholder register — institutional ownership here is dominated by index/large-cap mutual funds (e.g., UTI Nifty Next 50, Mahindra Manulife) and FIIs, not a marquee name.
strengths: Near debt-free balance sheet with debt-to-equity of ~0.04
ROCE of ~31% and ROE of ~24%, well above the chemicals sector median
Q1 FY27 underlying volume growth of 12.2% (Consumer & Bazaar) shows demand is not purely price-driven
Promoter holding of 69.18% with zero shares pledged
watchpoints: Vinyl acetate monomer (key raw material) cost up from ~$924/tonne to ~$1,370/tonne on the West Asia conflict, pressuring gross margin
Stock trades at ~57x earnings versus a chemicals sector median closer to 26x — priced for continued outperformance
Q2 FY27 results due 28 October 2026 will show whether Q1's margin recovery and volume growth held through the festive quarter
CFO transition underway (Amit Agarwal as CFO-designate from 9 Oct 2026) ahead of incumbent Sandeep Batra's 2027 retirement — succession risk looks low but execution continuity is worth tracking
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 (September 2026 quarter) results on 28 October 2026 — specifically whether underlying volume growth and EBITDA margin held up as VAM costs stayed elevated and fresh price hikes worked through the market.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked Q1 FY27 numbers (revenue, PAT, EBITDA margin, segment volume growth) across multiple news outlets and the company's own earnings presentation; figures were broadly consistent. P/E estimates varied by source (56x-69x) depending on timing/method — used the ~57x central estimate rather than averaging; the dispersion is noted, not resolved. Shareholding percentages (promoter 69.18%, FII/DII splits) taken from aggregator sites for the September 2026 quarter, not independently verified against the BSE/NSE corporate filing. Price, returns, dividend and split data were taken as given and not recomputed.
